title: Optimize CPU text shaping
body: I've been working on some editor optimizations, and ran into a couple places where text shaping ended up being a bottleneck. For instance, on editor startup (populating menu lists), or when switching to large scenes (`SceneTreeDock` calculating string heights). I optimized this by analyzing `SceneTreeDock` refreshes and editor launches to start with, and then built a custom testing scene so that reviewers could easily replicate the results. The project is just to replicate the bottlenecks I found in practice. In the test project there's a `TextServerOptimization.tscn` that consists of a Tree that constantly queues redraws of its 25000 everchanging elements. Here's the flamegraph for `_shape_lines` for that without this PR: And here's the flamegraph with this PR: We can compare before and after timings by using the amount of time spent in `hb_shape_full code` during shaping. Before this PR, 7.57% of shaping time was spent in `hb_shape_full` code. After this PR, 14.1% is. Since that function call wasn't changed and should be constant, that means that text shaping should be taking at most `(100 - 14.1) / 14.1 * 7.57 + 7.57 = 53.7%` of the time it was taking before. Put another way, in my tests CPU text shaping with this PR is 86% faster than on `master`! All of the changes fall into two categories: avoiding unnecessary dynamic allocations, and avoiding looking up font information we don't need to because the mutex checks aren't cheap even if it is cached. The `ScriptIterator`, `_font_is_script_supported`, and `reserve` changes are there to avoid allocations, while the cached font information and `FontPriorityList` are meant to avoid hitting the more expensive synchronized cache when we don't need to. The function level caching works well because fonts tend to be used in streaks, so it's mostly the same information getting looked up repeatedly. The `FontPriorityList` implements the same logic as before, but only ends up calling `_font_is_script_supported` and `_font_is_language_supported` on the minimum number of fonts needed. Thoughts on the `FontPriorityList` location and `friend` use is appreciated, I'm not sure what the preference is for that. Could move it to its own file, move the definitions to the .cpp, swap them to lambdas... --------------------- All performance tests were run on builds made with the following command: `scons optimize=speed_trace debug_symbols=yes platform=linuxbsd dev_build=no production=yes`. The test project: `TextServerOptimization.tscn` in [editor-optimization-test-scenes.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21709465/editor-optimization-test-scenes.zip)
